{{Short description|Uzbekistan female microbiologist}}

'''Dilfuza Egamberdieva''' is an Uzbekistan [[microbiologist]] specializing in [[agriculture]]. She is the CEO and founder of Ecobiome R&D Ltd. and serves as the head of the Biological Research and Food Safety Lab. Egamberdieva is notable for receiving the [[Carlos J. Finlay Prize for Microbiology|UNESCO-Carlos J. Finlay Prize]] for Microbiology, recognizing her significant contributions to the field. Her work focuses on developing microbial solutions to enhance soil and plant health in challenging environmental conditions, such as [[soil salinity]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dilfuza Egamberdieva |url=https://globalyoungacademy.net/degamberdieva/ |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Global Young Academy |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Elserafy |first=Menattalah |date=2023-09-11 |title=Dilfuza Egamberdieva, Uzbek scientist behind "super crops", wins UNESCO–Carlos J. Finlay Prize for Microbiology |url=https://www.unesco.org/en/articles/dilfuza-egamberdieva-uzbek-scientist-behind-super-crops-wins-unesco-carlos-j-finlay-prize |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=unesco.org}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Dilfuza Egamberdieva |url=http://www.stemwomen.asia/ |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=STEM Women Asia |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Egamberdieva was born in [[Uzbekistan]] and raised with four other siblings by her parents. Her family were large supporters of her education in science as she emphasized her country's prevailing belief for women to prioritize family over career and work.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Jewell |first=Wendy |date=2006-03-24 |title=Dilfuza Egamberdiyeva |url=https://myhero.com/Dilfuza_Egamberdiyeva_06 |access-date=2024-05-29 |website=myhero.com}}</ref>

== Education ==
She completed her undergraduate studies in biology at the [[National University of Uzbekistan]] (1988–1993), followed by earning her PhD in Agricultural Sciences from [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt University]] in [[Berlin]], [[Germany]] (1998–2000). She pursued postdoctoral research at various institutions including [[University of Helsinki|Helsinki University]] in [[Finland]], the [[University of Florence]] in [[Italy]], [[Manchester Metropolitan University]] in the [[United Kingdom|UK]], [[Leiden University]] in the [[Netherlands]], and the Centre of Agricultural Landscape Research in [[Germany]].<ref name=":1" />

== Career ==
In 2007, Egamberdieva established Ecobiome R&D, a research lab in Uzbekistan.<ref name=":1" /> She also founded the Central Asian Chapter of The Organization for Women in Science for the Developing World (OWSD) in [[Uzbekistan]] and served as its chair.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-04-23 |title=Central Asia National Chapter of OWSD launched |url=https://owsd.net/news/news-events/central-asia-national-chapter-owsd-launched |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=OWSD |language=en}}</ref> Additionally, she was elected as a team member in a working group on the internationalization of German research within the [[German Science and Humanities Council|German Council of Science and Humanities]] (WR).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr. Egamberdieva in working group on Internationalisation of German Research |url=https://www.zalf.de/en/aktuelles/Pages/LBG/Internationalisation.aspx |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=www.zalf.de}}</ref> In 2018, Egamberdieva was appointed to both the High-Level Panel of Experts on Food Security and Nutrition (HLPE) and the UN [[Committee on World Food Security]] (CFS) for the term spanning from 2018 to 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Former members of the HLPE-FSN |url=https://www.fao.org/cfs/cfs-hlpe/experts/former-members-of-the-hlpe-fsn/en |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=HLPE - High Level Panel of Experts |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Dilfuza Egamberdieva member at HLPE |url=https://www.zalf.de/en/aktuelles/Pages/PB2/HLPE-Projekts_online.aspx |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=www.zalf.de}}</ref> She holds the role of National Focal Point Representative for UNESCO-SEPAN (Science and Technology Policy Asian Network) and serves as a board committee member from 2021 to 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Egamberdieva, Dilfuza |url=https://twas.org/directory/egamberdieva-dilfuza |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=The World Academy of Sciences |language=en}}</ref> Egamberdieva is designated as the ambassador of the [[American Society for Microbiology]] in [[Uzbekistan]] and serves on editorial boards, including [[Elsevier]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=O'zMU olimasi AQSH mikrobiologiya jamiyatining O'zbekistondagi elchisi etib tayinlandi |url=https://uzreport.news/society/ozmu-olimasi-aqsh-mikrobiologiya-jamiyatining-ozbekistondagi-elchisi-etib-tayinlandi |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=UzReport.news |language=uz}}</ref> Her scholarly contributions include co-authoring 200 publications in peer-reviewed journals and authoring 6 books.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dilfuza Egamberdieva {{!}} Elsevier |url=https://www.elsevier.com/books-and-journals/book-series/dilfuza-egamberdieva |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=www.elsevier.com |language=en-us}}</ref>

== Research ==
Egamberdieva's research primarily revolves around the soil microbiome, demonstrating the potential of [[microbes]] to act as stimulators and control agents, offering an alternative approach to conventional [[Agrochemical|agrochemicals]] in hostile environments. Her work also extends to investigating plant stress tolerance, soil biology, and microbial diversity.<ref>{{Cite web |last=uz |first=Daryo |date=2023-09-11 |title=Uzbek microbiologist Dilfuza Egamberdieva receives UNESCO Carlos Finlay Prize |url=https://daryo.uz/en/2023/11/09/uzbek-microbiologist-dilfuza-egamberdieva-receives-unesco-carlos-finlay-prize |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Daryo.uz |language=en}}</ref> The overarching goal of her research is to provide safer alternatives to chemical pesticides and fertilizers in agriculture.<ref name=":2" /> Egamberdieva's efforts involve identifying and harnessing various beneficial microbes to enhance a plant's ability to adapt to its environment, analogous to the concept of immunization in humans, thereby promoting resilience to diseases and environmental stresses.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Salt-tolerant bacteria improve crop yields |url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2013/10/131006142707.htm |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=ScienceDaily |language=en}}</ref>

== Notable Awards ==

* Egamberdieva won UNESCO J. Finlay Prize for Microbiology in 11-14-2023.<ref name=":0" />
* The World Academy of Science Award in Agricultural Sciences (2012)<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-09-18 |title=2012 TWAS Prize winners announced |url=https://twas.org/article/2012-twas-prize-winners-announced?via=TwasNEWS |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=The World Academy of Sciences |language=en}}</ref>
* TWAS-TWOWS-SCOPUS Young Women Research Award (2009)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Malaysia Plays Host to Young Women Researcher Award |url=https://www.isaaa.org/kc/cropbiotechupdate/article/default.asp?ID=5016 |access-date=2024-06-01 |website=Crop Biotech Update |language=en}}</ref>
